name: HYDRA-UMC-DEV-SERVER
technologies: SQLite (durable task/state journal, from DS05 onward)
build: Ten-delivery plan (DS01-DS10, see this repository's own README Roadmap section): a reproducible development host (target platform: Raspberry Pi 5 or Compute Module 5, both 8GB, NVMe-booted) that hosts this ecosystem's source code, an isolated task/workspace runner for bounded programming/build/test work, and a durable queue coordinating with HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT's own incident lifecycle - never a new AI to train, never a replacement operating system, never itself the authority that decides a machine is safe. Real build: python -m build (see pyproject.toml).
deployment_target_note: "dev-server" is a new deployment_target value, not yet used elsewhere in this ecosystem's manifests (existing values: cm5, mobile, user-pc, wearable). It denotes a Raspberry Pi 5 / CM5 host dedicated to development and task execution - explicitly NOT the same physical role as "cm5" (the operational node that talks to real machines/robots). Documented here so HYDRA-UMC-UPDATER/the dashboard do not misread it as an operational CM5.
notes: Scaffolding v0.0.4 - DS01-DS04 of the 10-delivery plan (contracts, limits and a verifiable skeleton). DS01-DS03 only read and describe. DS01: state-ownership table + 17-relationship grouping + a real, tested configuration schema (config.py) whose default policy grants NO task deployment permission. DS02: validated remote-station profile + read-only host preflight + dry-run provisioning plan, never executed. DS03: conservative migration (migration.py) - hashes/classifies every file in a source checkout, records unpushed commits, plans each class into one of four provably-separate destinations, refuses a private file to a shareable root; the source is never touched. DS04: the first thing that executes - workspace.py refuses a path that escapes a per-task workspace (.., absolute, symlink-out) and refuses two tasks sharing one; recipe.py pins a revision and refuses any command not in the policy's own allowed_commands; runner.py runs that one allow-listed command in the isolated workspace with a SCRUBBED environment (no inherited *_TOKEN/*_KEY/*_SECRET/ANTHROPIC_*/GITHUB_*/SSH_*), under a bounded timeout, killing the whole process group on timeout or cancel - proven by a real test that spawns a child-of-a-child and confirms both die. It still deploys nothing. Injectable WorkspaceFs/ProcessLauncher seams keep the control tests off a real host. CLI: config / inventory / station / migrate / task subcommands. No durable queue, AI provider integration or OPS-AGENT wiring exists yet: DS05, DS06 and DS07 respectively.
